title: The Heaviest Level

concept.title: Sum the values of each level
body: Level order gives the nodes row by row. For each row add up the values, remember the **largest sum** and the **number of the row** where it was found. Rows are numbered from 1 at the root. When two rows have the same largest sum, the question asks for the **smallest** row number, so only replace the best row when the new sum is **strictly larger**.

body.code:
best_sum = None
best_level = 0
level = 0
row = [root]
while row:
    level += 1
    total = sum(node.val for node in row)
    if best_sum is None or total > best_sum:     # strictly larger keeps the earlier level on ties
        best_sum, best_level = total, level
    row = [child for node in row for child in (node.left, node.right) if child is not None]

body: The values can be negative, so the first row must not be compared with 0: start with "no best yet". The list comprehension builds the next row from the children of the current row.

statement: The root of a binary tree is at level 1, its children are at level 2, and so on. Print the smallest level number whose values have the largest sum.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of a tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The level sums are 1, 7, -1: level 2 has the largest sum.

hints: Process the tree row by row and add the values of each row.
Do not start the best sum at 0: sums can be negative.
Replace the best level only when a sum is strictly larger.

    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def best_level(root):
    best_sum = None
    best = 0
    level = 0
    row = [root]
    while row:
        level += 1
        total = sum(node.val for node in row)
        if best_sum is None or total > best_sum:
            best_sum, best = total, level
        row = [child for node in row for child in (node.left, node.right) if child is not None]
    return best

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()

print(best_level(build_tree(vals)))
